titulo: To look forward to: tener ganas de and estar deseando
subtitulo: Tengo ganas de verte, estoy deseando llegar.
regla: Tener (muchas) ganas de + infinitive = to feel like / to look forward to. Estar deseando + infinitive = to really look forward to, can't wait to.

bloques.texto: Spanish has two common ways to say _to look forward to_ doing something:

filas: _to feel like doing_ or _to look forward to doing_ (context decides)
a stronger wish: _to really look forward to, can't wait to_

bloques.texto: Never drop the **de** after **ganas**. Add **muchas** to make it stronger: **tengo muchas ganas de verte**.
**Estar deseando** is usually translated as _looking forward to_ or _can't wait to_, more than just _feel like_.
In Mexico, **estar deseando** sounds a bit formal; you'll more often hear **ya quiero…**, **me muero de ganas de…** or **no veo la hora de…**: **ya queremos verte**.
Tip: **ganas** are an appetite; **deseando** is counting the days.

lista.es: ==Tengo ganas de== comer tacos de pescado.
lista.en: I feel like eating fish tacos.

lista.es: ==Tengo ganas de== ver a Luisa; la última vez fue hace dos años.
lista.en: I'm looking forward to seeing Luisa; the last time was two years ago.

lista.es: ==Tengo muchas ganas de== empezar el nuevo curso.
lista.en: I'm really looking forward to starting the new course.

lista.es: Ahorita ==tengo muchas ganas de== un helado de chocolate.
lista.en: Right now I really feel like a chocolate ice cream.

lista.es: ==Estamos deseando== llegar al hotel y meternos a la alberca.
lista.en: We can't wait to get to the hotel and jump in the pool.
I was really looking forward to meeting that guy.
I can't wait for there to be waves.

filas.t: Tengo ganas de ver a Beto.

bloques.texto: Say it out loud, then open the answer.

lista.p: In Spanish: _I feel like going to the beach._
lista.r: Tengo ganas de ir a la playa.

lista.p: In Spanish: _We can't wait to see you._
